data.name: GitMissing
data.value: git was not found. Install Git for Windows and start RepoBoard again.

data.name: GitTimedOut
data.value: git {0}: no answer after {1} s, cancelled.
data.comment: {0} = the git command (commit, fetch …), {1} = seconds

data.name: NotARepository
data.comment: {0} = folder path

data.name: InvalidBranchName
data.value: “{0}” is not a valid branch name.
data.comment: {0} = the name typed

data.name: OperationFailed
data.comment: {0} = operation (Fetch, Pull …), {1} = git's message

data.name: Op_Diff
data.comment: Name of the operation that reads a file's changes (git diff), used in "{0} failed: …".

data.name: Op_StageHunk
data.comment: Operation: put one block of changes of a file into the index

data.name: Op_StageLines
data.comment: Operation: put the selected changed lines of a file into the index

data.name: Hunk_Incomplete
data.value: This hunk is cut off at the line limit of the diff and cannot be staged in parts. Stage the whole file instead.

data.name: Hunk_NotUtf8
data.value: This file is not UTF-8 – parts of it cannot be staged here. Stage the whole file instead.

data.name: Hunk_Changed
data.value: The file changed since its diff was shown – nothing was staged. Look at the new diff and try again.

data.name: Hunk_DiffDriver
data.value: This file is shown through a diff driver (textconv) – parts of it cannot be staged here. Stage the whole file instead.

data.name: Hunk_SpecialFile
data.value: Symbolic links and submodules cannot be staged in parts. Stage the whole file instead.

data.name: Hunk_TwoFiles
data.value: git shows this change as one file deleted and another one added – it can only be staged as a whole.

data.name: Hunk_SplitsLastLine
data.value: The last line of the file has no newline – select it together with the lines next to it.

data.name: CommitsOther
data.comment: {0} = number of commits

data.name: Fetched_Behind
data.comment: {0} = “3 commits”, {1} = upstream branch

data.name: NewOnUpstream
data.comment: {0} = “3 commits”, {1} = upstream branch

data.name: Pulled
data.comment: {0} = “3 commits”, {1} = branch

data.name: Updated
data.comment: {0} = branch

data.name: Pushed
data.comment: {0} = branch

data.name: PushedWithUpstream
data.comment: {0} = upstream branch

data.name: Committed
data.comment: {0} = first line of the commit message

data.name: CommittedAndPushed
data.comment: {0} = first line of the commit message

data.name: Switched
data.comment: {0} = branch

data.name: BranchCreated
data.comment: {0} = branch

data.name: AutoPullSkipped
data.comment: {0} = the reason (Blocker_…)

data.name: Blocker_Operation
data.comment: {0} = Operation_… (merge, rebase …)

data.name: Blocker_Diverged
data.value: the branch has diverged ({0} local, {1} remote) – merge or rebase it yourself
data.comment: {0} = commits only local, {1} = commits only on the upstream

data.name: Scan_AddedOther
data.comment: {0} = number of repositories

data.name: AutoSync_Paused
data.value: Auto-sync paused until you resume it or RepoBoard restarts.

data.name: Notify_TitleOne
data.comment: Title of a Windows notification. {0} = 1

data.name: Notify_TitleOther
data.comment: Title of a Windows notification. {0} = number of repositories

data.name: Notify_Line
data.comment: One line of a notification. {0} = repository name, {1} = what happened

data.name: Notify_More
data.comment: Last line of a notification. {0} = number of further messages

data.name: Op_RemoveWorktree
data.comment: Name of the operation that removes a linked worktree (git worktree remove), used in "{0} failed: …".

data.name: Worktree_Block_Changes
data.value: Has changed or new files – it stays.

data.name: Worktree_Block_Operation
data.value: A merge or rebase is unfinished in it – it stays.

data.name: Worktree_Block_UnreferencedCommits
data.value: Detached with commits no branch or tag contains – they would be lost, so it stays. Create a branch for them first.

data.name: Worktree_Block_Unknown
data.value: git could not read its state – it stays.

data.name: Worktree_IgnoredChanged
data.value: Ignored files came up since the question that git would delete with it – it stays. Ask again to see them.

data.name: Worktree_Removed
data.comment: {0} = folder path of the worktree (detached, no branch)

data.name: Worktree_RemovedBranchStays
data.comment: {0} = folder path of the worktree, {1} = its branch

data.name: Worktree_AddedMain
data.value: {0} is a worktree – its repository {1} goes on the board, the worktree shows below it.
data.comment: {0} = folder the user chose, {1} = folder of the main worktree

data.name: InvalidCommit
data.comment: {0} = the text that was given as a commit id

data.name: Amended
data.comment: {0} = first line of the new commit message

data.name: AmendedAndPushed
data.comment: {0} = first line of the new commit message

data.name: Amend_Pushed
data.value: the last commit is already on a remote branch – changing it would need a force push

data.name: Amend_Unknown
data.value: git could not tell whether the last commit was pushed – it stays as it is

data.name: Reverted
data.comment: {0} = short commit id, {1} = its subject

data.name: CherryPicked
data.comment: {0} = short commit id, {1} = its subject, {2} = the current branch

data.name: Pick_Merge
data.value: merge commits cannot be reverted or cherry-picked here

data.name: Pick_Unknown
data.value: git could not read the repository's state

data.name: Pick_Operation
data.value: a {0} is still in progress – finish or abort it first
data.comment: {0} = the unfinished operation (Operation_…)

data.name: Pick_Initial
data.value: the branch has no commit yet

data.name: Pick_Changes
data.value: only with no staged or changed files – commit or stash them first

data.name: Revert_NotInHead
data.value: the commit is not in the current branch

data.name: CherryPick_InHead
data.value: the commit is already in the current branch

data.name: CherryPick_Applied
data.value: the current branch already has this change (picked before)

data.name: Pick_Ignored
data.value: {0} is ignored here and would be overwritten without a word – move it away first
data.comment: {0} = path of the ignored file

data.name: CherryPick_Empty
data.value: nothing to pick: the branch already has this change (perhaps through a squash merge) – end the cherry-pick with “Skip”

data.name: Amend_HeadMoved
data.value: the last commit changed since its message was filled in – tick “Amend last commit” again

data.name: Op_Merge
data.comment: Operation: merge another branch into the current one

data.name: Op_Rebase
data.comment: Operation: replay the current branch's commits onto another branch

data.name: Op_Continue
data.comment: Operation: go on with a stopped merge, rebase, cherry-pick or revert

data.name: Op_Abort
data.comment: Operation: end a stopped merge, rebase, cherry-pick or revert and go back to the state before it

data.name: Op_Skip
data.comment: Operation: leave out the commit a rebase, cherry-pick or revert stopped at

data.name: Op_MarkResolved
data.comment: Operation: stage a conflicted file as resolved

data.name: Merged
data.comment: {0} = the merged branch, {1} = the current branch

data.name: Rebased
data.comment: {0} = the current branch, {1} = the branch it was rebased onto

data.name: Continued
data.comment: {0} = the operation (Operation_…)

data.name: Aborted
data.value: {0} aborted – back to the state before it
data.comment: {0} = the operation (Operation_…)

data.name: Skipped
data.comment: {0} = subject or short id of the skipped commit

data.name: Resolved
data.comment: {0} = path of the file

data.name: Merge_BranchGone
data.comment: {0} = branch name

data.name: Rebase_Pushed
data.value: the rebase would rewrite commits a remote already has ({0}) – pushing them again would need a force push
data.comment: {0} = number of commits (CommitsOne/CommitsOther)

data.name: Operation_Stopped
data.value: stopped – resolve the conflicts in the opened row, then “Continue” (or “Abort”): {0}
data.comment: {0} = git's message

data.name: Operation_Gone
data.value: no merge, rebase, cherry-pick or revert is in progress anymore

data.name: Operation_Changed
data.value: the {0} went on since you were asked – check it again
data.comment: {0} = the operation (Operation_…)

data.name: Operation_FilesChanged
data.value: files changed since you were asked – check the list again

data.name: Continue_Conflicts
data.comment: {0} = number of conflicted files

data.name: Continue_Unstaged
data.value: stage the changed files first – a rebase goes on only with all of them in the index

data.name: Skip_Merge
data.value: a merge has no commit to skip

data.name: Continue_Empty
data.value: nothing left to commit: the resolution kept none of the commit’s changes – end it with “Skip”

data.name: Add_Refused
data.comment: {0} = folder path, {1} = git's message (e.g. about safe.directory)

data.name: RemovedFromBoard
data.value: Removed from the board – the folder {0} stays.
data.comment: {0} = folder path

data.name: FolderMissing
data.comment: {0} = folder path

data.name: Op_Discard
data.comment: Operation: discard the unstaged changes of files (WP-06)

data.name: Op_Stash
data.comment: Operation: put the changes into a new stash entry

data.name: Op_ApplyStash
data.comment: Operation: apply a stash entry, keeping it

data.name: Op_PopStash
data.comment: Operation: apply a stash entry and drop it

data.name: Op_DropStash
data.comment: Operation: remove an entry from the stash list

data.name: Discard_NotInRepo
data.comment: {0} = file path

data.name: Discard_NoRecycleBin
data.value: new files cannot go to the recycle bin here – nothing was discarded

data.name: Discard_StashMessage
data.comment: Message of the stash entry that keeps discarded changes; {0} = the file paths, comma-separated, cut

data.name: Discard_RecycleFailed
data.value: the new files could not go to the recycle bin: {0}
data.comment: {0} = the reason from the system

data.name: Discard_RecycleFailedAfterStash
data.value: the changes are in the stash list as “{1}”, but the new files could not go to the recycle bin: {0}
data.comment: {0} = the reason from the system, {1} = message of the stash entry

data.name: Discarded_Recycled
data.value: Discarded – the new files are in the recycle bin

data.name: Discarded_Stashed
data.value: Discarded – the changes are kept in the stash list as “{0}”
data.comment: {0} = message of the stash entry

data.name: Discarded_Both
data.value: Discarded – the changes are kept in the stash list as “{0}”, the new files are in the recycle bin
data.comment: {0} = message of the stash entry

data.name: Stash_Conflicts
data.value: resolve the conflicts first – git cannot stash while files are conflicted

data.name: Stash_OnlyNew
data.value: only new files changed – tick “With new files” to stash them

data.name: Stash_Gone
data.value: the stash entry is gone – it was dropped or popped meanwhile

data.name: Stash_ApplyConflicts
data.value: applied with conflicts – the entry stays in the stash list; resolve the conflicts in the opened row

data.name: Stash_PopNotDropped
data.value: applied, but the entry could not be dropped from the stash list: {0}
data.comment: {0} = git's message

data.name: StashedAs
data.comment: {0} = message of the stash entry

data.name: StashApplied
data.value: Applied “{0}” – the entry stays in the stash list
data.comment: {0} = git's subject of the stash entry

data.name: StashPopped
data.comment: {0} = git's subject of the stash entry

data.name: StashDropped
data.comment: {0} = git's subject of the stash entry

data.name: Recycle_Failed
data.comment: {0} = the error code of the shell, e.g. 0x7C

data.name: Recycle_Cancelled
data.value: cancelled – nothing was deleted for good

data.name: StashApply_Conflicts
data.value: resolve the conflicts first – git applies a stash entry only without conflicted files
